# Sampling

From continuous time to a sequence of numbers, and what is lost on the way.

## Sampling a Sinusoid {kicker="Discrete time"}

A continuous-time signal is measured every $T_s = 1/f_s$ seconds:

$$
x[n] = x(nT_s) = A \cos\left(2\pi \frac{f}{f_s} n + \varphi\right)
$$

::: {.incremental}
- $f_s$ is the **sampling rate** in samples per second
- $f / f_s$ is the **normalized frequency** in cycles per sample
- Only $f / f_s$ matters once the signal is sampled
:::

## The Sampling Theorem {kicker="Nyquist"}

A signal with no energy above $f_\text{max}$ is fully determined by its samples [@nyquist1928; @shannon1949] if

$$
f_s > 2 f_\text{max}
$$ {#eq-nyquist}

::: {.callout-note}
Half the sampling rate, $f_s / 2$, is the **Nyquist frequency**. Anything above it folds back.
:::

## Aliasing, Interactively {kicker="Try it"}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof f = Inputs.range([0.2, 15], {value: 3, step: 0.1, label: "f (Hz)", width: 420})
fs = 8
alias = Math.abs(f - fs * Math.round(f / fs))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const W = 1000, H = 300, T = 1, x = (t) => 40 + (W - 60) * t / T, y = (v) => H / 2 - v * (H / 2 - 30);
  const curve = (g) => d3.range(0, T, T / 1000).map((t) => `${x(t)},${y(Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * g * t))}`).join(" ");
  const samples = d3.range(0, T, 1 / fs);
  return htl.svg`<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" width="100%" style="max-height:330px">
    <line x1="40" x2="${W - 20}" y1="${H / 2}" y2="${H / 2}" stroke="#9FB4C8"/>
    <polyline points="${curve(f)}" fill="none" stroke="#0B63B5" stroke-width="2.5"/>
    ${alias !== f ? htl.svg`<polyline points="${curve(alias)}" fill="none" stroke="#19B3C9" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-dasharray="8 6"/>` : ""}
    ${samples.map((t) => htl.svg`<circle cx="${x(t)}" cy="${y(Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * f * t))}" r="7" fill="#0A2A4F"/>`)}
  </svg>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`Sampled at *f*<sub>s</sub> = ${fs} Hz, a ${f.toFixed(1)} Hz sinusoid ${alias === f ? "is captured correctly" : `looks like **${alias.toFixed(1)} Hz** (dashed)`}.`
```

## Computed When Rendered {kicker="Python"}

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
fs, f, N = 8, 9, 512                        # change f and render again
x = np.cos(2 * np.pi * f / fs * np.arange(N))
freqs = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, 1 / fs)
X = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(x * np.hanning(N)))
f_alias = freqs[np.argmax(X)]
```

A `{python} f` Hz tone sampled at `{python} fs` Hz peaks at **`{python} f"{f_alias:.1f}"` Hz** (@fig-spectrum). The
figure and this sentence come from Python code inside this slide in `talk.qmd`: change `f` there.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-spectrum
#| fig-cap: "Spectrum of the sampled tone, computed with NumPy."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 14, "axes.edgecolor": "#9FB4C8", "text.color": "#0A2A4F",
                     "axes.labelcolor": "#0A2A4F", "xtick.color": "#0A2A4F", "ytick.color": "#0A2A4F"})
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 3.4))
ax.plot(freqs, X / X.max(), color="#0B63B5", lw=2.5)
ax.axvline(fs / 2, color="#19B3C9", ls="--", lw=2)
ax.text(fs / 2, 0.9, "  Nyquist", color="#19B3C9")
ax.set(xlabel="Frequency (Hz)", ylabel="|X| (normalized)", xlim=(0, fs / 2 + 0.5))
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
```

# Filtering

The simplest way to remove what the samples cannot represent.

## A Moving-Average Filter {kicker="FIR"}

Averaging $M$ samples is a low-pass FIR filter:

$$
y[n] = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{k=0}^{M-1} x[n-k]
\qquad
|H(e^{j\omega})| = \left| \frac{\sin(M\omega/2)}{M \sin(\omega/2)} \right|
$$

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof M = Inputs.range([1, 16], {value: 4, step: 1, label: "M", width: 420})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const W = 1000, H = 240, x = (w) => 40 + (W - 60) * w / Math.PI, y = (v) => H - 25 - v * (H - 45);
  const mag = (w) => w === 0 ? 1 : Math.abs(Math.sin(M * w / 2) / (M * Math.sin(w / 2)));
  const pts = d3.range(0, Math.PI, Math.PI / 600).map((w) => `${x(w)},${y(mag(w))}`).join(" ");
  return htl.svg`<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" width="100%" style="max-height:260px">
    <line x1="40" x2="${W - 20}" y1="${H - 25}" y2="${H - 25}" stroke="#9FB4C8"/>
    <text x="${W - 20}" y="${H - 5}" text-anchor="end" font-size="16">ω = π</text>
    <polyline points="${pts}" fill="none" stroke="#0B63B5" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  </svg>`;
}
```

## Take-Home Messages {kicker="Summary"}

- Sampling keeps only the **normalized frequency** $f/f_s$
- Sample faster than **twice the highest frequency** (@eq-nyquist), or filter first
- A moving average is the simplest **low-pass filter**; longer means narrower

::: {.notes}
Ask the audience which frequency a 9 Hz tone sampled at 8 Hz appears at.
:::
